def: A system in which a language model repeatedly chooses actions or tools, sees the results and decides what to do next until it finishes or a limit stops it.
A system in which the programmer fixes the sequence of steps in code, and the model only fills in individual steps such as writing a summary.
The cycle of asking the model, running the tools it requested, appending the results to the conversation and asking again.
A function the surrounding program offers to a model, which the model can request but never runs itself.
A small typed piece of a message, such as text, a tool_use request or a tool_result, that together make up one turn.
The way per-step failure rates multiply over a long task: n steps each succeeding with probability p succeed together with probability p to the power n.
A program that, given text, produces more text one token at a time; on its own it can only write.
A stand-in model that replays replies written in advance so that example code and lab checks run offline with identical output every time.
